Whether it’s a transmission issue, a diesel engine needing repair, an electrical system malfunction or driveshaft repair, we have the tools and skills to get the job done right! | View Our Repair Services | Frequently Asked Questions | What is fleet maintenance management? | Fleet maintenance management is a comprehensive approach to keeping a company’s fleet of vehicles in optimal operating condition. This process involves scheduling regular inspections, performing preventative maintenance, and addressing repairs promptly to ensure that every vehicle is safe, reliable, and ready to serve the business’s needs. Effective fleet maintenance management helps businesses minimize downtime, reduce operational costs, and extend the lifespan of their vehicles. At Grease Pro, we understand the importance of a well-maintained fleet to your business operations. We offer managed fleet service appointments and accept a variety of fleet management cards, making the maintenance process easy and efficient for businesses and their employees. | What are your fleet maintenance services? | At Grease Pro, our fleet maintenance services cover a wide range of needs to keep your vehicles running smoothly and reliably. Our services include preventative maintenance such as oil changes, tire rotations, and brake repairs, as well as more comprehensive repairs like transmission issues, electrical system malfunctions, and driveshaft repairs. We aim to provide a one-stop solution for all your fleet maintenance needs, ensuring your vehicles spend less time in the shop and more time on the road. Our certified professionals are equipped to service a variety of industries and vehicle types, from pest control to A/C companies and cleaning services. With the convenience of managed fleet payment options and online loyalty accounts, Grease Pro offers the ultimate service and convenience for your fleet maintenance requirements. | How often should fleet vehicles be serviced? | Fleet vehicles typically require servicing every 3,000 to 5,000 miles to ensure they remain in peak operating condition. This frequency allows for regular inspections and tune-ups that can significantly extend the lifespan of the vehicles and prevent costly breakdowns. At Grease Pro, we tailor our fleet maintenance services to meet your specific needs, helping you avoid unnecessary “over-maintenance.” Our team uses an inspection checklist to identify any potential issues and performs services based on your drivers’ reports and our expert assessment. Whether it’s a transmission issue, a diesel engine needing repair, an electrical system malfunction or driveshaft repair, we have the tools and skills to get the job done right! | View Our Repair Services | Frequently Asked Questions | What is fleet maintenance management? | Fleet maintenance management is a comprehensive approach to keeping a company’s fleet of vehicles in optimal operating condition. This process involves scheduling regular inspections, performing preventative maintenance, and addressing repairs promptly to ensure that every vehicle is safe, reliable, and ready to serve the business’s needs. Effective fleet maintenance management helps businesses minimize downtime, reduce operational costs, and extend the lifespan of their vehicles. At Grease Pro, we understand the importance of a well-maintained fleet to your business operations. We offer managed fleet service appointments and accept a variety of fleet management cards, making the maintenance process easy and efficient for businesses and their employees. | What are your fleet maintenance services? | At Grease Pro, our fleet maintenance services cover a wide range of needs to keep your vehicles running smoothly and reliably. Our services include preventative maintenance such as oil changes, tire rotations, and brake repairs, as well as more comprehensive repairs like transmission issues, electrical system malfunctions, and driveshaft repairs. We aim to provide a one-stop solution for all your fleet maintenance needs, ensuring your vehicles spend less time in the shop and more time on the road. Our certified professionals are equipped to service a variety of industries and vehicle types, from pest control to A/C companies and cleaning services. With the convenience of managed fleet payment options and online loyalty accounts, Grease Pro offers the ultimate service and convenience for your fleet maintenance requirements. | How often should fleet vehicles be serviced? | Fleet vehicles typically require servicing every 3,000 to 5,000 miles to ensure they remain in peak operating condition. This frequency allows for regular inspections and tune-ups that can significantly extend the lifespan of the vehicles and prevent costly breakdowns. At Grease Pro, we tailor our fleet maintenance services to meet your specific needs, helping you avoid unnecessary “over-maintenance.” Our team uses an inspection checklist to identify any potential issues and performs services based on your drivers’ reports and our expert assessment. It is important to replace damaged CV boots before they lead to further damage. | CV Joint Replacement | Regular use can wear on CV Joints, impacting your vehicle’s operation. Its main function is to connect your vehicle’s transmission to the wheels. The ‘constant velocity’ aspect of its name refers to its unique job of maintaining a constant drive force to the wheels, regardless of the angle of the joint. This means whether your car hits a pothole or drives over uneven terrain, the CV joint ensures smooth power delivery without any variations in speed or force, keeping your ride stable and controlled. | What are bad CV joint symptoms? | A common symptom of a bad CV joint is a loud clicking or ticking sound when turning, often due to metal-on-metal contact inside a worn joint. Another visible sign is grease on the inside of your wheel, indicating a torn CV boot. You might also experience vibrations in your steering wheel that worsen with speed, a sign of an aging CV joint losing its lubrication. A knocking or clunking sound when accelerating or reversing can also be a signal of a CV joint issue. If you notice any of these symptoms, then it’s time for a check-up, as they can also stem from other suspension components, and getting a proper diagnosis is essential to get the right repairs. | How do you tell the difference between a bad wheel bearing and a bad CV joint? | Distinguishing between a bad wheel bearing and a bad CV joint can be tricky. Generally, a faulty CV joint will make a clicking noise when turning, while a bad wheel bearing typically causes a constant humming or growling noise that increases with speed. | What is a driveshaft? | In simple terms, a drive shaft is a crucial component that transmits the engine’s torque to the wheels, essentially getting your car moving. It’s a rod-like part that connects the transmission to the wheels, playing a pivotal role in your car’s ability to drive. Without a functioning drive shaft, the power from your engine wouldn’t effectively make its way to the wheels, leaving your car immobile. | How to measure driveshaft length for driveshaft replacement? | Measuring driveshaft length involves measuring from the center of the front U-joint to the center of the rear U-joint. However, keep in mind there are various factors that can affect this measurement, such as the type of vehicle and specific setup. It’s often best to consult a professional for accurate measurement and replacement to ensure proper balance and alignment. | Can a driveshaft be repaired? | Yes, a driveshaft can often be repaired, especially if the damage or wear is minor. Common repairs include balancing, replacing U-joints or CV joints, and fixing any bends or breaks. These repairs can extend the life of your driveshaft and are a cost-effective alternative to complete replacement. | What causes drive shaft failure? | Drive shaft failure is generally due to wear and tear from regular use. Components like U-joints and CV joints undergo a lot of stress and will likely need replacement as a car ages. Common causes of failure include worn-out U-joints or CV joints, imbalance, damage from impacts, or not keeping up with regular maintenance. Remember, regular inspections and timely repairs can go a long way in preventing sudden and dangerous failures. | What is an axle? | An axle is essentially a steel rod that connects to your car’s wheels. It’s crucial because it takes the power from your car’s transmission and transfers it to the wheels, allowing your vehicle to move. The axle acts as a bridge, playing an essential role in steering, driving, and braking. cooling system repair? Your vehicle’s cooling system is crucial to the engine’s health. Old antifreeze, damaged cooling fans, and cracked fan belts can lead to overheating and even engine failure. Regular maintenance of your cooling system can prevent the need for radiator replacement and other major engine repairs. For all of your cooling system repair needs - turn to the team at Grease Pro. | Cooling System Flush & Fill | Your vehicle’s cooling system is essential for maintaining engine temperatures and ensuring the health of key engine components. A routine cooling system flush is crucial for maintaining your vehicle’s performance and avoiding more costly cooling system repairs . | Learn About Cooling System Flush | Cooling System Pressure Test | Cooling system repairs begin by identifying leaks. A leak in your cooling system needs to be caught as soon as possible. Left untreated, a small leak can lead to more extensive damage. | Learn About Pressure Test | Radiator Replacement | Has your engine’s temperature gauge been elevated? Is coolant puddling beneath your car? These are telltale signs your vehicle’s radiator needs attention. Putting off serious cooling system repairs can leave you stranded. | Learn About Radiator Replacement | GreasePro proudly serves Lynn Haven, Callaway, Panama City, Panama City Beach and Chipley areas . We offer the best services with trained industry professionals with years of experience who you can trust to repair your cooling system . Visit one of our many convenient locations near you or schedule a service that works with your time on our website. | How do you check your coolant level? | Checking the coolant level in your car is a simple but important task. First, ensure your car is on a level surface and the engine is cool. Open the hood and locate the coolant reservoir – it’s usually a transparent container with markings for “Min” and “Max” levels. Look at the level of the liquid against these marks. If the coolant is below the “Min” line, it’s time to add more. Remember, it’s crucial not to open the radiator cap when the engine is hot, as it can be extremely dangerous due to the pressurized hot steam and liquid. | How do you add coolant to a car? | Adding coolant to your car is a straightforward process. First, make sure the engine is cool, and the car is parked on a level surface. Locate the coolant reservoir under the hood – it’s usually a clear tank with a colorful cap. Slowly remove the cap (only when the engine is cool) to release any built-up pressure. Then, add the correct type of coolant for your vehicle – you can find this information in your car’s manual. Fill the tank to the “Max” line, but be careful not to overfill it. After adding, securely replace the cap and close the hood. | How do you fix a coolant leak? | Fixing a coolant leak involves identifying where the leak is coming from and addressing the specific issue. Common sources of leaks include radiator hoses, the radiator itself, or the water pump. For instance, if it’s a cracked hose that’s causing the leak, replacing the hose is the most effective solution. Components in the cooling system can wear out over time, so it’s key to replace old or damaged parts as needed. However, identifying and fixing coolant leaks can sometimes be complex, and it’s often best handled by professionals. At Grease Pro, we can help track down the exact source of the leak and fix it properly to ensure your car stays cool and runs smoothly. | Does coolant evaporate? | Yes, coolant can evaporate, particularly in hot conditions. When your car is exposed to high temperatures, the coolant’s volume can gradually decrease due to evaporation, affecting the efficiency of the cooling system. There are several factors that can contribute to this: High temperatures can accelerate the rate of evaporation; leaks in the cooling system can lead to a gradual loss of coolant; a defective radiator cap might not maintain proper pressure, resulting in increased evaporation; and an improper mix of coolant and water can cause the coolant to evaporate more quickly than normal. It’s important to regularly check the coolant level and the overall condition of the cooling system to prevent issues related to evaporation. | How much coolant do I need? | The amount of coolant needed for your car depends on the model and size of its engine. Typically, a car’s cooling system can hold between 5 and 15 liters of coolant. The best way to know for sure is to check your car’s manual for the exact capacity. Remember, it’s important to use the right type of coolant and to mix it with water in the correct proportions as specified by your vehicle manufacturer. If you’re unsure, at Grease Pro, we can help determine the right amount and type of coolant for your car and ensure it’s filled correctly. | How do you pressure test a cooling system? | To pressure test a cooling system, you’d use a cooling system pressure tester. This tool attaches to the radiator, replacing the cap, and you manually pump it until the pressure matches what’s indicated on your radiator cap (usually between 13-16 psi for modern vehicles). After pressurizing, let the car sit for about 20-30 minutes. During this time, inspect the system for leaks and monitor the pressure gauge for any drop in pressure, which could indicate a leak. If you’re not comfortable performing this test or don’t have the equipment, we at Grease Pro can | conduct a thorough pressure test | for you. It’s often better to have a professional handle this to ensure an accurate diagnosis and to avoid potential damage to the cooling system. | What are signs you need a coolant flush? | Recognizing when your car needs a coolant flush is key to keeping your engine in good shape. You might need a coolant flush if your vehicle’s temperature gauge is showing more fluctuation than usual, suggesting issues with coolant circulation. Change? | Regular oil changes are vital to maintaining the health and longevity of your vehicle’s engine. Oil helps lubricate the engine’s moving parts, reducing friction and preventing wear and tear over time. Our expert technicians at Grease Pro can provide you a | fast and easy walk-in oil change | , and our blog will answer some common questions about oil changes and share some tips for keeping your engine running smoothly. | How Often Should You Change Your Oil? | The frequency of oil changes depends on various factors, such as the type of vehicle, driving conditions, and oil type. Generally, most car manufacturers recommend | changing your oil every 5,000-7,500 miles | , or every six months to a year if you drive fewer miles. However, newer vehicles may have longer oil change intervals of up to 10,000-15,000 miles. | It’s crucial to follow your vehicle’s recommended oil change intervals and not try to determine how many miles you can go over an oil change, for the health of your car. Over time, oil can break down and become contaminated with dirt, debris, and other particles. This can reduce its effectiveness in lubricating the engine and protecting it from damage. If you go too long without changing your oil, the oil can become thick, sludgy, and gummy, which can clog up the engine and cause it to run less efficiently. | What Happens If You Go Too Long Without an Oil Change? | Not changing your oil regularly can lead to a variety of issues for your vehicle. Without proper lubrication, the metal parts in your engine can rub against each other, causing friction and heat buildup. This can lead to increased | wear and tear on the engine components | , including the pistons, crankshaft, and bearings. Eventually, this can lead to engine damage and failure. | Another issue that can arise from not changing your oil is decreased engine performance. As the oil becomes thicker and less effective, the engine may have to work harder to operate, leading to decreased fuel efficiency and reduced power output. Going too long without an oil change can lead to costly repairs and maintenance down the road. In extreme cases, engine damage from lack of oil can be irreversible and require an engine replacement. | Tips for Maintaining Your Vehicle’s Oil | While | regular oil changes are crucial | , there are several other things you can do to maintain your vehicle’s oil between oil change intervals. Here are some tips from GP to help keep your vehicle running smoothly: | Check your oil level regularly: It’s essential to check your oil level at least once a month, especially if you’re driving frequently or taking long trips. This will help you catch any potential problems early on and prevent damage to your engine. | Use high-quality oil: Choosing the right type of oil can make a big difference in the performance and longevity of your engine. Look for high-quality oils that meet or exceed the manufacturer’s recommendations. | Keep your engine clean: Dirt and debris can accumulate in your engine over time, which can cause your oil to become contaminated. Regularly cleaning your engine can help prevent this from happening. | Replace your oil filter regularly: Your oil filter is responsible for removing impurities from your oil, which can help keep your engine running smoothly. Be sure to replace your oil filter at the recommended intervals. | Regular oil changes are a vital part of vehicle maintenance that should not be ignored. By sticking to your recommended oil change intervals and ensuring that your vehicle’s engine is properly lubricated, you can help prolong the life of your engine and save yourself from costly repairs down the road. So, the next time your vehicle is due for an oil change, make sure to take the time to get it done with the expert technicians at Grease Pro – your car (and wallet) will thank you! for Your Car | Keeping your car’s engine running smoothly requires more than just filling up the gas tank. | Regular oil changes | are crucial to ensure the longevity and efficiency of your engine. Here are five essential things you should know about oil changes to keep your car in top shape. | 1. Why Oil Changes Are Important | Motor oil is the lifeblood of your car’s engine. It lubricates the engine’s moving parts, reduces friction, and helps to prevent overheating. Over time, oil breaks down and becomes less effective at protecting your engine. Regular oil changes remove the old, degraded oil and replace it with fresh, clean oil, helping to extend the life of your engine and maintain performance. | 2. How Often Should You Change Your Oil? | The age-old question: “How often should you change your oil?” The answer depends on several factors, including the type of oil you use and your driving habits. Traditional wisdom suggested changing oil every 3,000 miles, but with modern engines and advanced oil formulations, many vehicles now have recommended intervals of 5,000 to 7,500 miles. Always consult your car’s owner’s manual for the manufacturer’s recommendations. | 3. Choosing the Right Oil for Your Car | Not all motor oils are created equal. Your car’s engine is designed to work with a specific type of oil, whether it’s conventional, synthetic, or a blend. Synthetic oil changes often come at a higher cost but provide better performance and protection, particularly in extreme temperatures. To determine what kind of oil your car needs, check your owner’s manual or consult with an | oil change service | professional. | 4. The Cost of an Oil Change | The cost of an oil change can vary based on several factors, such as the type of oil used—whether conventional, synthetic, or a blend—and the specific needs of your vehicle, especially if it requires specialized oils for advanced or high-performance engines. How to Avoid Them | One of the most important aspects of vehicle maintenance is | keeping your tires in good condition | . Not only does proper tire care improve your car’s performance, it also helps to keep you safe on the road. One common problem that can occur with tires is tread wear. This occurs when the rubber on the tire wears down, eventually leading to a blowout. In this blog post, we will discuss the five main causes of tire tread wear and how to avoid them. | 1. Driving on Rough Roads | One of the most common causes of tire tread wear is driving on rough or unpaved roads. The uneven surface of these roads can cause the tire to flex and bend, which wears down the tread over time. If you must drive on an unpaved road, make sure to go slow and avoid any large potholes or rocks that could damage your tires. | 2. Overinflated Tires | Another common cause of tire tread wear is overinflation. When a tire is inflated to more than the recommended pressure, it puts extra stress on the sidewalls and tread. This can cause the tread to wear down prematurely. Always check your owner’s manual or the placard on your door jamb to see what the recommended tire pressure is for your vehicle. | 3. Underinflated Tires | Conversely, if your tires are underinflated, this can also cause tread wear. When a tire is not inflated to the proper pressure, it puts extra stress on the center of the tread. This can cause the tire to wear down in the middle first, eventually leading to a blowout. Always check your tire pressure regularly and inflate to the recommended pressure when necessary. | 4. Misaligned Wheels | If your wheels are out of alignment, this can also cause premature tread wear. When a wheel is misaligned, it causes the tire to rub against the road surface unevenly. This will wear down the tread on one side of the tire more than the other, eventually leading to a blowout. You can tell if your wheels are out of alignment, if your car seems to pull to one side when you’re driving or if your tires are wearing unevenly. If you suspect your wheels are out of alignment, take your car to the Grease Pro nearest you to have them checked and adjusted as necessary. | 5. Worn Suspension Components | Another common cause of tire tread wear is worn suspension components. When shocks or struts become worn, they can’t absorb bumps as well, which puts extra stress on the tires. This will cause the tread to wear down prematurely. If you notice that your car is bouncing more than usual or that the ride is rougher than it used to be, | have your suspension checked by a mechanic. | These are just some of the most common causes of tire tread wear. By being aware of them, you can help to prevent premature tread wear and extend the life of your tires. If you do experience tread wear, bring your car to Grease Pro for | all your tire service, repair, and replacement needs | . Services | Off-Road | Modification | Car & Truck Sales | Offers | Promotions | Gift Cards | Events | Blog | Video Gallery | Schedule a Service | How to Stop Windshield From Fogging Up | There’s nothing more frustrating than a foggy windshield when you’re trying to drive, especially in cold or rainy weather. You turn on the heat to defog it, but then you’re stuck sweating in a box of hot air. Rolling down the windows just makes things worse by letting in the cold. So, what can you do? Luckily, there are simple solutions to stop your windshield from fogging up—without turning your car into a sauna. | Why Does My Windshield Fog Up? | Before we dive into solutions, let’s talk about why this happens in the first place. Your windshield fogs up because of condensation—moisture in the air inside or outside your car hitting the glass and turning into tiny water droplets. | Inside Fog: Warm, moist air from your breath, wet clothes, or even your car’s heater meets the cold windshield. | Outside Fog: Cold air outside meets the warmer windshield, causing moisture in the air to condense on the outside surface. | Understanding the cause makes it easier to stop car windows from fogging up in winter or rainy weather. | A Fogged Interior Windshield | If your windshield fogs up from the inside, try these simple fixes to clear it up and keep it from coming back: | Use the Air Conditioner – Even in winter, the AC helps remove moisture from the air inside your car. Turn on your defroster with the AC to clear up fog quickly. | Turn Off Recirculation – Fresh air from outside is drier than the humid air inside your car. Switch off recirculation mode to bring in fresh air. | Keep Windows Clean | – Dirt and oil trap moisture, making fogging worse. Clean your windshield regularly with a glass cleaner to reduce buildup. | DIY Anti-Fog for Windshield – A simple hack is to apply a thin layer of shaving cream on your windshield, then wipe it off. This leaves a film that prevents condensation. | Absorb Excess Moisture – Leave silica gel packs or a sock filled with cat litter in your car to absorb humidity. | A Fogged Exterior Windshield | Fogging on the outside of your windshield can be just as frustrating. Here are some ways to prevent it and maintain a clear view: | Warm Up Your Car First | – Let your defroster and heater warm up the windshield before driving to balance the temperature difference. | Use an Anti-Fog Windshield Treatment – Special anti-fog products for windshields create a hydrophobic layer that prevents fog buildup. | Apply Rain Repellent | – Products like Rain-X help moisture bead up and roll off, reducing outside fogging. | Don’t Wipe with Your Hands – Your hands leave oil on the glass, making fogging worse. Use a clean microfiber cloth instead. | Prevention | For a long-term solution to foggy windows, follow these preventative measures to keep moisture under control: | Check for Leaks | – Moisture buildup inside your car could be from a leak. Make sure your doors and windows seal properly. | Change Your Cabin Air Filter | – A clogged air filter holds moisture, leading to more fogging. | Crack a Window Slightly – Allowing some airflow helps equalize temperature and reduce condensation. | Expert Help for a Fog-Free Drive | Don’t let a foggy windshield put your safety at risk. Change Services in Panama City | Your vehicle’s transmission may not always be top of mind, but it plays a crucial role in delivering power from the engine to the wheels. Just like any other major component of your car, the transmission requires regular maintenance to perform its best. Ignoring it can lead to noticeable issues like rough gear shifts or unusual noises, which are signs that it’s time for a check-up. | That’s where Grease Pro comes in. We’re dedicated to ensuring that your transmission receives the attention it needs through our specialized transmission fluid change services. Just like oil changes or other maintenance tasks, regular changes of your transmission fluid can prevent a lot of common transmission problems, helping you avoid costly repairs down the line. While prioritizing this maintenance might not be the highlight of your day, we’re here to help make it as easy as possible. | Understanding Transmission Fluid and Its Importance | What is Transmission Fluid? | Transmission fluid is a critical component in your vehicle, primarily serving as the lifeblood of the transmission system. But what exactly is a transmission? Essentially, it’s a complex system that converts the engine’s power into a controllable force that drives your wheels. Transmission fluid ensures that this system’s gears operate smoothly by lubricating them, which prevents grinding. It also acts as a coolant, protecting the transmission from overheating under stress—whether that’s during a prolonged drive or stop-and-go traffic. This fluid isn’t just any lubricant; it’s specially formulated to withstand the pressures of transmission operations, whether you’re using automatic transmission fluid (ATF) or another type tailored to your vehicle’s needs. | Why Change Your Transmission Fluid? | The importance of regular transmission fluid changes goes beyond routine vehicle maintenance; it directly impacts the longevity and efficiency of your car: | Protect Your Gears: Think of transmission fluid as protective gear for your car’s internal components. Fresh fluid is rich in additives that safeguard the metal surfaces inside your transmission, much like how high-quality oil preserves an engine. This protection is crucial to avoid the costly wear and tear that can lead to major mechanical failures. | Maintain Peak Performance: Old, contaminated fluid can cause your transmission to hesitate or perform inconsistently. Regularly changing your transmission fluid ensures that gear shifts remain smooth and responsive, allowing your vehicle to perform at its best whenever you accelerate. | Avoid Costly Repairs: Regular fluid changes are an investment in your vehicle’s health, helping to clear out debris and prevent the accumulation of damaging sludge. By maintaining clean fluid, you ensure that your transmission operates efficiently, avoiding the expensive repairs that come with neglected maintenance. | At Grease Pro, we’re committed to enhancing your driving experience by providing your vehicle with the best possible care. We tailor our transmission services to meet the specific needs of your vehicle, ensuring it receives the appropriate type of fluid and all the benefits that come with our expert maintenance. | When to Change Your Transmission Fluid | Regularly changing your transmission fluid is vital to ensure your vehicle continues to operate efficiently and reliably. But how do you know when it’s time to schedule this service? Understanding the general guidelines and recognizing the warning signs can help you take proactive steps to maintain your transmission’s health. | Signs You Need a Transmission Fluid Change | Your vehicle will often tell you when it’s time to consider changing the transmission fluid through a few telltale signs: | Gear Slippage : If your transmission is slipping between gears or seems to struggle with finding the right gear, it could be a sign that the fluid is no longer effective. | Delayed Engagement : When you shift from park to drive, there should be an immediate response. If there’s a noticeable delay, it’s a clear indicator that your transmission fluid needs attention. | Unusual Noises: Whining, clunking, or humming sounds from your transmission when you’re driving are not normal and often suggest that the fluid isn’t lubricating the gears adequately. | Transmission Overheating: If your transmission temperature warning light comes on, it could mean the fluid is too old to cool and lubricate the system effectively, leading to overheating. | General Guidelines for Transmission Fluid Change | While the specific interval can vary based on your vehicle type and usage, here are some general guidelines to consider: | Mileage-Based Changes: Many manufacturers recommend changing your transmission fluid every 30,000 to 60,000 miles. However, if you frequently drive in harsh conditions—such as in heavy traffic, in extreme climates, or while towing—this interval should be shorter. | Visual and Smell Checks: Regularly check your transmission fluid’s color and odor. Fresh fluid is typically a bright red color and has a slightly sweet smell. If your fluid turns brown or black or smells burnt, it’s time to change it. | Manufacturer’s Recommendations: Always refer to your vehicle’s owner’s manual for the most accurate guidance on transmission maintenance schedules. | How to Change Transmission Fluid | While the process of changing transmission fluid is relatively straightforward, actually completing it can often be messy and somewhat tedious. Here’s how it’s typically done: | Draining the Old Fluid: The first step involves removing the old, contaminated fluid. This is usually done by removing the transmission pan or using a drain plug, allowing the old fluid to flow out. | Replacing the Filter: Many vehicles also require a transmission filter change during the fluid change process. The filter captures debris and contaminants, and replacing it helps ensure the cleanliness and efficacy of the new fluid. | Refilling with New Fluid: After the old fluid is drained and the filter replaced, new transmission fluid is added to the correct level as specified by the vehicle’s manufacturer. It’s crucial that the type of fluid used matches the specifications for your vehicle to ensure proper function and avoid damage. | Simplify Your Transmission Maintenance with Grease Pro | Changing your transmission fluid can be a messy, inconvenient task. That’s why Grease Pro is here to help, with 8 locations throughout Panama City, FL, and the surrounding areas. Our experienced technicians handle the complexities of transmission maintenance, not only replacing old fluid with high-quality new fluid but also ensuring responsible disposal to protect both your car and the environment. | For those seeking a reliable transmission fluid change in Panama City and or the surrounding areas, we hope to be your local choice. Our goal is simple — make transmission maintenance straightforward and stress-free so you can drive with confidence. Have questions or need advice on transmission care? Our knowledgeable team is ready to assist. | Frequently Asked Questions | How can I check my transmission fluid? | Checking your transmission fluid involves parking your vehicle on a level surface, applying the parking brake, and then running the engine. With the engine running, you can pull out the transmission fluid dipstick, wipe it clean, reinsert it, then pull it out again to check the level. It’s essential to note that the process may vary based on your vehicle’s make and model, and some newer vehicles do not have a dipstick. If you’re unsure, we at Grease Pro would be happy to help you check it. | What color should my transmission fluid be? | Healthy transmission fluid generally has a bright, clear red color and a slightly sweet smell. If it’s brown or black or has a burnt smell, it’s likely time for a fluid change. If you’re unsure about the condition of your transmission fluid, Grease Pro is here to assist you. | How much would a new transmission cost? | The cost of a new transmission varies widely, depending on the make and model of your vehicle, the type of transmission, and whether you’re considering a new or rebuilt transmission. For the most accurate estimate, we recommend | contacting our service team | . | How much transmission fluid do I need for my car? | The amount of transmission fluid your car needs will depend on the vehicle’s make, model, and transmission type. It typically ranges from 6 to 10 quarts. For the most accurate information, please refer to your vehicle’s owner manual or reach out to us at Grease Pro. | How often should I change my transmission fluid? | Generally, it’s a good idea to change your transmission fluid every 30,000 to 60,000 miles. However, this can vary based on your vehicle’s make and model, and your driving conditions. Please consult your vehicle’s owner manual for the manufacturer’s recommendation. | What could cause my transmission fluid to leak? | Transmission fluid leaks can be caused by several issues, including worn-out seals or gaskets, a damaged fluid line, or a corroded transmission oil pan. If you notice a leak or find a bright red liquid under your vehicle, | bring your car to Grease Pro | for an inspection. | How can I tell if my transmission is going bad? | Symptoms of a failing transmission may include difficulty shifting gears, unexplained noises, a burning smell, or the check engine light coming on. If you’re experiencing any of these signs, we recommend bringing your vehicle to Grease Pro for a diagnostic test. | How long does it take to replace a transmission? | The time it takes to replace a transmission can vary greatly depending on the type of transmission and the vehicle. Generally, it could take anywhere from a few hours to a few days. For a more accurate estimate, please | contact our team | at Grease Pro. | How much does a transmission weigh? | The weight of a transmission depends on the make and model of the vehicle and the type of transmission. A transmission can weigh anywhere from about 100 to 400 pounds. | What exactly is a transmission flush? | A transmission flush is a maintenance process where all of the oil in a transmission is removed, new oil (and sometimes cleaning solutions) is run through it to help remove grime and sludge, and then it is filled up with new oil. It’s a way to help extend the life of your transmission and improve its performance. If you’re interested in | this service | , our team at Grease Pro would be happy to assist. | Your vehicle’s transmission may not always be top of mind, but it plays a crucial role in delivering power from the engine to the wheels. Just like any other major component of your car, the transmission requires regular maintenance to perform its best. Ignoring it can lead to noticeable issues like rough gear shifts or unusual noises, which are signs that it’s time for a check-up. | That’s where Grease Pro comes in. We’re dedicated to ensuring that your transmission receives the attention it needs through our specialized transmission fluid change services. Just like oil changes or other maintenance tasks, regular changes of your transmission fluid can prevent a lot of common transmission problems, helping you avoid costly repairs down the line. While prioritizing this maintenance might not be the highlight of your day, we’re here to help make it as easy as possible. | Understanding Transmission Fluid and Its Importance | What is Transmission Fluid? | Transmission fluid is a critical component in your vehicle, primarily serving as the lifeblood of the transmission system. But what exactly is a transmission? Essentially, it’s a complex system that converts the engine’s power into a controllable force that drives your wheels. Transmission fluid ensures that this system’s gears operate smoothly by lubricating them, which prevents grinding. It also acts as a coolant, protecting the transmission from overheating under stress—whether that’s during a prolonged drive or stop-and-go traffic. This fluid isn’t just any lubricant; it’s specially formulated to withstand the pressures of transmission operations, whether you’re using automatic transmission fluid (ATF) or another type tailored to your vehicle’s needs. | Why Change Your Transmission Fluid? | The importance of regular transmission fluid changes goes beyond routine vehicle maintenance; it directly impacts the longevity and efficiency of your car: | Protect Your Gears: Think of transmission fluid as protective gear for your car’s internal components. Fresh fluid is rich in additives that safeguard the metal surfaces inside your transmission, much like how high-quality oil preserves an engine. This protection is crucial to avoid the costly wear and tear that can lead to major mechanical failures. |

It does not identify a specific failed part. The cause may involve an electrical connection, a sensor, a component that controls engagement, or a mechanical problem. | Our technicians use the warning, your vehicle’s symptoms, and diagnostic findings to determine what needs further testing. For more detail about the dashboard message, read our guide to | what “Service 4 Wheel Drive” means | . | Four-Wheel Drive Services We Provide | 4WD System Inspection | We inspect the transfer case, hubs, and related driveline components for signs of wear, damage, and fluid leaks. We inspect their condition and operation, then recommend cleaning, lubrication, adjustment, or repair as appropriate for the hub design and the findings. | Transfer Case Repair | The transfer case distributes power between the front and rear driveline in many four-wheel drive vehicles. Some vehicles use sensors inside the wheels to measure pressure directly. Others use wheel-speed information to detect changes that can indicate an underinflated tire. | A warning does not automatically mean a sensor has failed. Low pressure, a tire leak, a system fault, or an incomplete relearn can require different solutions. Our guide to | why your TPMS light is on | explains the warning in more detail. | When to Have Your TPMS Checked | A TPMS check can help when: | The light remains on after the tires have been inflated to the vehicle’s recommended pressure. | A tire pressure reading is missing or appears incorrect. | The warning flashes before staying illuminated. | The light returns after tire service or a sensor replacement. | A reset does not resolve the warning. | If a tire repeatedly loses pressure, the tire itself also needs attention. Clearing a warning will not repair an air leak. | Do You Need a TPMS Reset or a New Sensor? | TPMS Reset and Relearn | Depending on the vehicle, the system may need recalibration or a relearn after tire rotation, sensor replacement, or other tire service. We follow the procedure required for your vehicle so the system can recognize the correct information. A reset is performed after the underlying pressure or service issue has been addressed. | Tire Pressure Sensor Replacement | A damaged or failed sensor may need replacement. In many direct TPMS systems, the sensor has a sealed battery, so battery failure requires replacing the sensor assembly. We test for the source of the warning before recommending replacement and program or relearn compatible sensors as required. | What Affects TPMS Sensor Replacement Cost | The cost depends on your vehicle, the sensor it uses, how many sensors need attention, and the programming or relearn work required. A pressure adjustment and a sensor replacement are different services. Testing helps us explain which work your vehicle needs and the recommended next step. | How We Check Your Tire Pressure Monitoring System | Check pressure and symptoms. We start with the warning you are seeing and compare tire pressure with your vehicle’s specifications. | Test the system. Depending on the system, we check sensor responses and diagnostic information to identify faults or communication problems. | Recommend the appropriate service. A sensor or communication fault is another possibility. Checking pressure and testing the system helps identify the cause. | Does a flashing TPMS light mean a bad sensor? | A light that flashes before staying on commonly indicates a TPMS malfunction. A failed sensor is one possible cause, but testing is needed to determine which part of the system needs attention. Check your owner’s manual for your vehicle’s warning pattern. | Can you replace one TPMS sensor? | A single failed sensor can often be replaced without replacing every sensor.
